question: In which language did Aryabhata write the book titled Aryabhatiyam?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanskrit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Aryabhatiyam** is an ancient Indian mathematical and astronomical treatise.
 
• It was written by the mathematician and astronomer Aryabhata in the **5th century AD**.
 
• The text is composed in **Sanskrit**, which was the scholarly language of ancient India.
 
• Aryabhatiyam covers topics such as arithmetic, algebra, plane trigonometry, and spherical trigonometry, and continues to be a significant work in the history of mathematics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sanskrit:**

 
 
• Sanskrit is an ancient Indo-European language of India in which the oldest scriptures of Hinduism, the Vedas, were composed.
 
• It is known for its rich literary tradition and has been used in various scholarly and religious texts throughout Indian history.
 
• Modern Indian languages like Hindi, Marathi, Bengali, and many others have evolved from or have been influenced by Sanskrit.
 
• Sanskrit is also used in classical music, dance, and other cultural expressions in India.
 
 
 
• **Aryabhata:**
 
 
• Aryabhata was an Indian mathematician and astronomer who lived during the 5th century AD.
 
• He is best known for his work Aryabhatiyam, which includes various innovations in mathematics and astronomy.
 
• Aryabhata introduced the concept of zero and place value system, which are fundamental to modern mathematics.
 
• He also calculated the value of pi (π) and explained the concept of the Earth's rotation, which were groundbreaking contributions at the time.
 
 
 
• **Aryabhatiyam:**
 
 
• The Aryabhatiyam is divided into four chapters: Gitikapada (cosmology), Ganitapada (mathematics), Kalakriyapada (time calculations), and Golapada (spherical astronomy).
 
• The text uses a decimal place value system and includes various methods for solving algebraic equations.
 
• It also discusses the motion of celestial bodies and eclipses, reflecting Aryabhata's deep understanding of astronomy.
 
• Aryabhatiyam has been studied and commented upon by various scholars over the centuries, making it a cornerstone of Indian mathematical and astronomical tradition.
